summary.headline: Sundram Fasteners Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 30% YoY, driven by OE and exports; EBITDA margin fell to 15.7% on raw material inflation.
summary.overview: Management reported about 30% revenue growth in Q2 FY27, led by OE, with exports up 57% YoY (about 10 points from currency and about 47% from volume and dollar terms). Steel and aluminium inflation in Q1 and Q2 compressed contribution margin by roughly 2.5-3%, which took Q2 EBITDA margin to 15.7% and H1 to 15.9%. Management said the brunt of the RM hit is already in the P&L and expects H2 margins to expand as export mix rises. Operating cash flow looked weak, which management attributed to working capital build from longer export cycles, GST input credit and inflated RM inventory.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR140 crore in corresponding quarter
About 10 points from FX, balance volume and dollar terms
Down from about 25% last year, earlier about one-third
Recorded for the quarter, not H1
Management says in line with operations

segments.name: OE (domestic)
segments.commentary: Growth driven by car and M&HCV segments per management; OE pricing pass-through is generally immediate, with some customers on a lag now reset to about 1 month.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Up 57% YoY in Q2 and about 40% in H1; key customers Cummins and Navistar schedules improved. Export EBITDA is above 20% per management, but export pricing has no RM pass-through and absorbed much of the cost hit.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 10% of business; prices raised in aftermarket prospectively depending on competitive intensity.

segments.name: Non-auto (wind, aerospace, rail)
segments.commentary: Non-auto at 35-37% of revenue. Wind to exceed about INR500 crore annual revenue after phase 3 investment of INR70-80 crore. Aerospace at INR50 crore last year, targeted INR100 crore+ this year, INR200 crore later, with INR30-40 crore capex.

segments.name: EV (Stellantis, US)
segments.commentary: Revenue expected INR150-175 crore this year vs about INR50 crore last year; plug-in hybrid and ICE portion billing started. Peak volume visibility expected by H2 next year.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: China subsidiary grew 25-30% in INR terms (10-12% local currency); UK subsidiary grew 20%+ in INR terms. Management says both are profitable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth expected to be almost the same as H1 (about 25%) across OE, retail and exports; H2 growth seen mirroring H1 per current indications.
Domestic performance expected up about 3-5% in H2. Cars and SUVs: low double digit growth; M&HCV and LCV: mid-teens; tractors: below 10%, around 6-7%, with a bias to 5%.
EBITDA margin expected to expand in H2 as export share rises and RM prices cool; management did not quantify the recovery.
FY27 capex on course to complete the INR400 crore program, possibly slightly higher depending on customer requirements.
FY28 capex indicated at INR350-450 crore per year; more precise guidance after Q3. FY28 revenue guidance called premature.
Cash flow expected to improve as borrowings moderate and working capital normalises.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex: INR281 crore spent so far against INR400 crore program; completion on course, possibly slightly higher.
FY28 capex indicated at INR350-450 crore per year (indicative, to be refined after Q3).
Wind energy: third phase of investment ongoing, targeting over INR500 crore annual wind revenue; investment about INR70-80 crore.
Aerospace: INR30-40 crore investment in testing and other equipment to move toward INR200 crore revenue.
Railways: existing capacity used to service current orders; no separate investment planned.
Asset utilisation improved substantially, lowering depreciation as a percentage of revenue.
demand_pricing: OEMs give a 1-month firm schedule and 2 months indicative; continued schedules available across domestic and export segments.

Class 8 (US): cumulative preliminary orders of 353,000 units in past 12 months; US retail Class 8 down 5% YTD September, expected to end the year up 3-5%. Projection of 232,000 trucks challenged, with some estimates at 210,000-220,000.
EPA 2027: heavy-duty engine life deferred by 3 years; NOx limit tightened from 200 to 35 mg/bhp with a non-compliance penalty option; pricing still a grey area.
Domestic tractor demand expected to soften in Q3 and moderate in Q4 due to base effect and uneven monsoon (IMD forecast 88-112% of normal).
Domestic MHCV grew 21% and LCV 27% in H1 (CV combined 25%).

qa_highlights.question: How and when will the 400-500 bps gross margin decline seen at Indian OEMs flow through to the company, and is there further downside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the brunt is already in the P&L; pass-through is mostly immediate in OE, with some customers on a 3-month lag now reset to 1 month. Export and aftermarket carry the uncompensated impact. Further impact only if RM prices rise again.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Export cycles can stretch to 9 months, raising inventory and receivables. Input GST credit piled up due to subcontracting and inflated RM purchases, plus capex. Management expects borrowings to moderate and cash flow to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any increase in FY27 capex and what is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is on course to complete the INR400 crore program, possibly slightly higher. FY28 indicated at INR350-450 crore per year, with guidance after Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth match H1, and how should margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 growth expected to mirror H1 (about 25%). Margins to expand in H2 mainly from higher export share. Tonnage growth 15-16% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Gas and fuel cost impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas and HSD-linked fuel prices peaked at INR200+ per unit from sub-INR100 and moderated to about INR150, still above pre-March 2026 levels. Management said the impact is negligible on margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a metric for new product development?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal guideline: parts developed in a year should generate 20% of revenue over development period plus next 3 years; management says performance is in line with plan.

risks_watch: RM inflation (steel, aluminium, fuel and indirect materials): export and aftermarket cannot recover cost; margin recovery depends on RM prices cooling.
Working capital and cash flow: borrowings rising; watch whether receivables, inventory and GST credit normalise in Q3.
Tractor and rural demand softness in H2 due to uneven monsoon.
US Class 8 demand: retail down 5% YTD, pricing grey area under EPA 2027 norms.
EV revenue ramp (INR150-175 crore) and peak volume visibility only by H2 next year.
FY28 capex (INR350-450 crore) and revenue guidance deferred to Q3.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, exports and H2 growth, but cautious on margins and FY28, deferring FY28 guidance as premature. Answers on cash flow and gas costs were brief and partly deflected, and the call had a connectivity break that delayed marketing-related answers.

It is already there in our P&L.

So that will be negligible, sir.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Further margin hit only if RM prices rise again, export and aftermarket cannot pass through cost, domestic tractor demand softens in Q3 (IMD 88-112% of normal) and EV revenue guide cut to INR150-175 crore.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: US Class 8 order momentum

rows.why: Operating cash flow weak from export cycles up to 9 months, GST input credit build and inflated RM inventory; management expects borrowings to moderate, but answers were brief and partly deflected.

rows.why: Non-auto share rose to 35-37% of revenue from about 30%, with wind to exceed INR500 crore annual revenue and aspiration of 50%, but no timeline was given.
